page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highcpu-32 is a compute-oriented virtual server powered by the x86_64 AMD EPYC 9B45 processor. The instance provides 32 dedicated vCPUs distributed across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU configuration features 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, complemented by hardware acceleration flags including AVX-512, AVX-VNNI, SHA-NI, and AES encryption instructions. System memory totals 60.0 GB, resulting in an allocation ratio of 1.88 GB per vCPU.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-core CPU capabilities and compression performance. In stress-ng single-core tests and Geekbench evaluation, the instance scores within the top 10 percent of recorded results. Software compilation using Clang, ray tracing, and static web serving benchmarks demonstrate upper-quartile execution speeds. Cryptographic tests and extended vector instructions also perform in the top 25 percent. Conversely, multi-core stress tests, raw memory bandwidth across large blocks, and database transactions show average throughput.

The instance includes no bundled local storage, meaning that all persistent disk storage must be provisioned independently via networked block volumes. No complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default, and there are no hardware GPUs. Because memory capacity is limited to 1.88 GB per vCPU, the server offers high CPU resource density per cost tier for calculation-bound workloads, but introduces constraints for memory-intensive caching or in-memory databases.

Workload suitability centers on tasks that prioritize raw CPU clock cycles and multi-threaded processing over large memory footprints. Google Cloud Platform c4d-highcpu-32 is appropriate for continuous integration and compilation pipelines, static web traffic handling, data compression and decompression utilities, batch media processing, and CPU-based lightweight machine learning inference.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highcpu-32 is a compute-focused virtual machine configured with 32 dedicated vCPUs and 60 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 1.88 GB of RAM per vCPU. Powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9B45 processor spanning 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, the instance includes 32 MB of L3 cache alongside hardware support for AVX-512, AVX-VNNI, and cryptographic instruction sets. The server does not bundle local disk storage or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring remote network storage for persistent data. In standardized performance benchmarks, the instance demonstrates top-tier single-core computation, data compression, and text processing, accompanied by strong compiler execution and static web serving throughput. Database operations and large-block memory transfers register at mid-tier levels, reflecting its lower memory-to-core allocation. Google Cloud Platform c4d-highcpu-32 is well aligned for CI/CD build pipelines, code compilation, microservice clusters, batch compute jobs, and lightweight CPU-based machine learning inference.
